**About Us**
------------

Lorikeet is redefining what customer support looks like — and we're just getting started.

We build AI that handles complex, high-volume support for fintechs, healthtechs, marketplaces, and delivery services. Not chatbot-tier AI. The kind that actually resolves tickets, gives support teams their time back, and raises the bar for what software can do.

We're backed by over $50M USD from QED, Blackbird, and Square Peg, with backing from operators like Claire Hughes Johnson (ex-Stripe COO) and Cristina Cordova (Linear COO), plus founders of Canva, Atlassian, and Airwallex. We're the first company since Canva to be funded at early stage by all three of Australia's top VC funds — which tells you something about the calibre of people who've looked closely at what we're building and said yes.

Our customers include some of the largest telehealth, fintech, and marketplace companies in the US and Australia — many handling over a million support tickets a year. The problems are real, the scale is real, and the work matters.

If you want to build something that genuinely changes how businesses and customers interact — this is the place.

**About the role**

Our Forward Deployed team works between our customers and our product. They take a customer’s whole support operation (the tickets, the systems, the policies) and turn it into AI agents that resolve real customer queries in production.

As an FDE intern, you’ll be part of that team from day one, not on a side project. The workflows you build will go live and handle real conversations for some of the largest fintech and healthtech companies in the US and Australia. You’ll have close support from the team and real ownership of the work you take on.

Day to day, you’ll:

* Dig into customers’ support tickets and data to find where AI can fully resolve queries, and where it can’t yet
* Build, test, and refine AI workflows from first draft through to production
* Help connect workflows to customer systems through APIs, and test integrations before they go live
* Join customer calls, share what you’ve found, and own defined parts of an implementation
* Use Claude Code and other AI tools to speed up analysis, build internal tooling, and improve how the team works

You’ll leave knowing how AI agents are deployed end to end at scale in regulated industries. You’ll also have hands-on skills in workflow design, API integrations, testing and evaluation, and LLM fundamentals, and experience turning a customer’s messy real-world problem into a working solution.

**We’d love to talk if you**

* Are curious and learn fast. You pick up new tools quickly and enjoy figuring things out.
* Are technically confident. You don’t need to be a software engineer, but you’re comfortable reading API docs and working with data.
* Sweat the details. You notice when something’s off, ask good questions, and follow through.
* Communicate clearly with technical and non-technical people alike.
* Are genuinely interested in AI. It’s a bonus if you’ve experimented with LLMs or built something with AI tools on your own.

**What's unique about this opportunity?**
-----------------------------------------

**A culture that's genuinely different.** Low ego, high trust, no tolerance for talented jerks. We work efficiently, keep hours flexible, and actually mean it — because life outside work matters. We're committed to building a diverse team and actively encourage applicants from underrepresented backgrounds. We care far more about user obsession and eagerness to learn than traditional credentials.

**A front-row seat to building something meaningful.** We're Series A and moving fast. You'll have real scope to shape the product and the company — not just execute someone else's vision.

**Performance recognized in real time, not on a calendar.** Promotions happen when you're ready — leadership meets every six weeks specifically to identify and recognize strong performers, so you're never waiting for an arbitrary review window to move up.

**We're AI-native, and we'll make you AI-native too.** Every person at Lorikeet uses AI in their day-to-day work (current favourite: Claude Code), with unrestricted access and no usage limits. You'll leave with skills that matter for the next decade of work.

**Twice a year, the whole company flies to Hawaii.** Headquartered in Sydney, with teams spanning the US and UK — which means getting everyone in the same place is something we invest in seriously. We spend the time hacking on ideas, building things together that wouldn't otherwise exist, and making memories that remind you why you joined a startup in the first place.

**A recruitment process built on respect, not hoops.** We keep it simple: a couple of informal chats to share our story and hear yours, followed by a paid ~two-day work trial. The work trial is genuinely the best part — you'll work on real problems alongside the actual team, get a true feel for how we operate, and we'll both come out of it knowing whether this is the right fit. No trick questions, no take-homes that disappear into a void. Just real work, done together.

If you're from an underrepresented background and don't tick every box, please reach out anyway. We know firsthand that diverse teams perform better, and we're proud that our team reflects a broad spectrum of identities and lived experiences.

------------

Capabilities include radionuclide metrology, measurement and monitoring of radioactivity in the environment, low and intermediate radioanalytical chemistry and nuclear forensics.

This position will be based in the Low Level Radioanalytical Group which maintains measurement capabilities to quantify naturally occurring radionuclides and difficult to measure radionuclides through alpha, beta and gamma measurement techniques, as well as lead-210 dating of sediments.

***Use your molecular biology skills to help detect cancer earlier through liquid biopsy research***

A single tube of blood can carry traces of a tumour long before conventional tests find it. Liquid biopsy is reshaping how cancer is detected, monitored and treated, and the quality of that science rests on meticulous sample handling and reliable laboratory data. As a Research Assistant in the cancer research team at Macquarie Medical School, you will help generate exactly that.

Working within the Faculty of Medicine, Health and Human Sciences, you will process and analyse human biological samples, contribute to the investigation of circulating tumour-derived biomarkers and molecular features of cancer, and help build the datasets that underpin publications and future clinical translation. Structured training will be provided in liquid biopsy methodologies and related molecular biology techniques, so you can extend your technical repertoire while contributing from day one.

This is a valuable opportunity for an early-career researcher with a foundation in molecular biology who enjoys precise bench work and wants to grow within a research-intensive environment. You will work closely with the lead researcher and wider cancer research team, with access to modern laboratory facilities, professional development programs and a research community spanning biomedical, translational and health services domains.

**About the Role**

Reporting to the Deputy Dean, Research and Innovation and working under appropriate supervision, you will provide technical and research assistance across the cancer research program. Your responsibilities will include:

  

* Performing routine laboratory procedures and molecular biology techniques in line with established protocols and standard operating procedures
* Receiving, processing, aliquoting and storing biological samples, including blood-derived specimens, with close attention to sample integrity and traceability
* Undertaking training in liquid biopsy methodologies and contributing to the analysis of circulating tumour-derived biomarkers and other molecular analytes
* Assisting with nucleic acid extraction, quality assessment and preparation of samples for downstream molecular analyses, including sequencing applications
* Recording, organising and maintaining experimental and sample data in laboratory records, databases and electronic systems, with appropriate version control
* Assisting with quality control, preliminary data processing, targeted literature searches and the preparation of datasets, figures, tables, reports and manuscripts
* Identifying and reporting protocol deviations, technical issues or unexpected results, and maintaining laboratory areas, equipment and reagents in line with research governance, ethics, biosafety and WHS requirements

We're a family-owned early education provider with an **unbroken 13-year record of exceeding the National Quality Standards,** placing us in the top 5% of private Long Day Care providers nationally. Our services operate across **NSW and the ACT**, and we're expanding.

What makes 360 different isn't a slogan. It's what actually happens in our rooms:

* The **THRIVE Program** develops executive function, self-regulation and social skills from birth — grounded in research, built on relationships
* **Beyond the Classroom** takes children into the world — bush school, swim school, the Australian Museum, project-driven excursions designed and led by our teachers
* Our **Creative Arts program** brings in working artists and uses dance, drama and creative expression as genuine tools for learning
* **STEM** treats children as scientists from birth, fostering wonder, creativity and innovation every day
* Our **Literacy program** puts language everywhere — because we believe a love of reading starts before a child can hold a book

We recruit across multiple levels. Tell us where you are, and we'll talk about where you could go.

**Assistant Educator** — Enrolled in or holding a Certificate III. You're building your skills in a room alongside experienced educators, contributing observations, supporting children through routines, and learning from a team that genuinely invests in the people around them.

Not sure which level fits? Apply and tell us where you're at. We'll take it from there.

**What life looks like at 360**

**Pay and conditions** Salaries are paid above award across all roles, in line with the Federal Government's Worker Retention Payment. Your qualification level and responsibilities are reflected in your classification from day one, with progression as you grow.

**What makes the work sustainable**

* Additional educators in every room — you're supported, not the only one carrying it
* Generous non-contact time built into your week, not squeezed from the edges of your day
* Monthly RDOs and leave over Christmas and New Year
* Subsidised childcare for your own children within 360 services

**Your career, actively supported**

* A structured induction and a buddy from your first day
* Formal check-ins at 2–4 weeks, 3 months and 6 months — so you always know where you stand and what support is available
* Access to the **360 Learning Platform (Ed App)** and a full professional development calendar
* A genuine internal pathway — from Assistant Educator through to Room Leader, Educational Leader, Nominated Supervisor, and beyond. Half our leadership team has grown from within

*"My growth at 360 has taken me from a graduate Early Childhood Teacher to a room leader to — five years later — a part-time university lecturer."* — Sheryl Ho, former 360 educator

**What we're looking for**

Across every role, the qualities that matter most to us are the same:

* **A genuine commitment to child safety** — not as a box to tick, but as a professional and personal standard that shapes every interaction with children
* **Curiosity about children** — how they think, what they notice, and what they're working out about the world
* **Warmth and reliability** — children need consistent, familiar faces. So do good teams
* **A reflective mind** — you don't need all the answers, just the willingness to keep seeking them
* **Collaboration** — because the best things we do at 360, we do together

**Pre-employment screening**

Because children's safety is our paramount priority, all successful applicants will be required to complete the following before commencing:

* **Working With Children Check** (NSW) or **Working With Vulnerable People registration** (ACT), verified before your first day. You must notify 360 immediately in writing if your check status changes at any time
* **National Police Check** — as a broader screening measure complementing the WWCC, required for all child-related roles
* **Prohibited persons register check** via the NQA ITS
* **Qualification verification** — all qualifications independently checked, including ACECQA approval status and RTO validity
* **Two structured verbal reference checks** conducted directly with your previous supervisors or colleague.
* **Signed Declaration of Disciplinary and Investigative History** and acknowledgement of your Child Safe Code of Conduct obligations
* **Mandatory national child safety training**, to be completed during induction. All ECEC workers are required to complete the foundation modules by commencement.

Please also note that personal devices are not permitted while working directly with children at any 360 service.

**About Us**
  
Nepean Blue Mountains Local Health District (NBMLHD) is an exceptional environment to advance your career while enhancing your skills and expertise. As a recognised leader in the healthcare industry, we deliver a comprehensive range of public health services across the Nepean, Blue Mountains, and Lithgow Regions.
  
  
The Primary Care and Community Health Unit consists of 9 centres that provide a range of services for children, young people and their families, adults, older people and their carers. Our services range from health promotion, prevention and early detection through to assessment, treatment and continuing care. Our staff work in partnership with schools, GPs, hospitals, non-government agencies and other organisations to provide care across our centres, in people’s homes, other community venues as well as virtual care (telehealth).
  
  
Join the Supportive and Palliative Care team in a rewarding Clinical Nurse Specialist (CNS2) role where you will provide senior clinical leadership and contribute to the delivery of high-quality, person-centred care for patients with life-limiting illnesses and their families. Based at Hawkesbury Community Health Centre, this role provides care and support to supportive and palliative care patients across the community and Hawkesbury Hospital, with opportunities to contribute to services across other areas of Nepean Blue Mountains Local Health District.
  
  
As a key member of the multidisciplinary team, you will utilise advanced clinical skills and exercise a high level of professional autonomy to support the development of specialist clinical practice and service delivery within the Supportive and Palliative Care service. Working closely with managers, medical staff and other senior clinicians, you will help ensure patients and carers receive safe, compassionate and coordinated care throughout their healthcare journey.
  
  
The successful incumbent will be responsible for coordinating care across the continuum of supportive and palliative care services, including community, inpatient and outpatient settings. This role focuses on the management of patients with complex care needs, facilitating effective care planning, clinical coordination and communication between healthcare providers to promote seamless transitions and positive patient outcomes.
  
  
This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced and motivated nurse to take on the next step in their career and make a meaningful difference in the lives of patients, families and carers. Apply today!
  
  
**Benefits available to eligible NBMLHD employees**

* Opportunity for extra tax savings through Salary Packaging
* Novated Leasing
* Great education opportunities through Education Training Service which offers over 110 courses each year
* Access to our Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for staff and family members
* Fitness Passport

**What you will bring to the role**

* Current registration as a Registered Nurse Division 1 with the Australian Health Practitioners Regulation Authority AHPRA.

* Relevant post-registration qualifications (Palliative Care) and at least 3 years’ experience working in the clinical area of their specified post-graduate qualification, or such other qualifications or equivalent experience deemed appropriate (Supportive & Palliative Care).

* Demonstrated capacity to provide effective nursing care that is person centred, family inclusive and culturally sensitive to people accessing health services.

* Demonstrated ability to perform in a clinical leadership role and use critical thinking as it relates to the delivery of advanced evidenced based nursing care.

* Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively with patients, family/carers and a diverse range of health care providers with effective communication written, verbal and interpersonal skills.

* Demonstrated commitment to professional development.

* Ability to work independently with minimal supervision maintaining involvement within the wider multidisciplinary team
